cards.text: Jesus is standing by the Lake of Gennesaret, and the crowd is pressing in on Him to hear the word of God. PRESSING in! I spent years squeezed into a junk drawer, and even I'd be looking for an exit.
Then He spots two boats at the edge of the lake. The fishermen have left them and are washing their nets.

cards.question: Jesus climbs into one of those two boats at the edge of the lake. Whose boat is it?
Jesus asks Simon, the fisherman who owns the boat, to take Him all the way across the lake.
Simon puts out a little from shore. Then Jesus sits down in the boat and ___ the people.

cards.text: Jesus finishes speaking. Then He turns to Simon and says, “Put out into deep water and let down your nets for a catch.”

cards.question: Simon and the other fishermen were washing their nets when Jesus showed up. What does Simon tell Jesus about the night they just had?

answers.text: We worked hard all night and caught nothing
We sold our whole catch before sunrise
A storm kept us on shore all night

cards.question: Simon's night was a bust, but he'll let the nets down anyway. He says he'll do it because ___ says so.

cards.text: So down go the nets into the deep water, after a whole night of nothing. Friend, after ONE burnt batch I need a nap and a pep talk.

cards.question: Simon lets the nets down in the deep water, and they come up empty again, just like last night.
Simon's nets are so full of fish they begin to tear. So they signal to their ___ in the other boat to come and help.
The partners come over, and they fill both boats so full of fish that the boats begin to ___.
Luke calls him Simon Peter here. When he sees this catch, what does he do?

answers.text: He runs to tell the crowd

cards.question: Simon Peter is down at Jesus' knees. What does he say to Jesus?

answers.text: Go away from me Lord because I'm a sinful man
Stay with us Lord and fish with us forever
Teach me Lord how to find fish like that

cards.text: Simon's companions are astonished at the catch, and so are his partners James and John, the sons of Zebedee. A whole crew of professional fishermen, standing knee-deep in fish with their mouths hanging OPEN.

cards.question: Simon just asked Jesus to go away from him. Jesus answers by telling Simon not to be afraid.
Then Jesus tells Simon what's ahead. What will Simon be doing from now on?
The fishermen bring their boats ashore and stay behind to sell the big catch before anything else.

cards.text: They left EVERYTHING and followed Him, right after a catch that nearly sank two boats. That's me pulling the best batch of my life out of the oven and walking out the door without even boxing it up.

findings.problem: Simon first appears in this passage as an answer option on a choice card. No earlier card says who he is. Card 4 calls him 'the fisherman who owns the boat,' but only after the baker has already had to pick his name.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: The right answer stands out. Jesus is the only person who has just spoken to Simon. James and Zebedee haven't appeared yet, so a baker can rule them out at once. The question tests nothing and doesn't look like the other answers.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike.

findings.problem: The question says 'this catch' and 'Luke calls him Simon Peter here.' Both point back to earlier cards that are no longer on screen. The question never says what the catch was (two boats so full of fish they begin to sink).

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: The wrong answer 'Stay with us Lord and fish with us forever' reads as silly, and its tone doesn't match the right answer's. That makes the right answer easy to spot by tone alone.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.
